# Corporate Security
Corporate Security protects Company personnel, property and research. Security staff turn out in regulation appearance at all times. A guard who looks professional is rarely asked to prove it.
## General Security - [bold]Security Trainee[/bold]: probationary guard. - [bold]Security Officer[/bold]: guard. - [bold]Senior Security Officer[/bold]: experienced guard. Leads patrols. - [bold]Security Sergeant[/bold]: head of site security. Commands the guard detail and reports to the senior employee on site.
## Personal Protection Close protection for senior executives. It answers to the Personal Protection Coordinator, and through them to the executive being protected. - [bold]Personal Protection Officer[/bold]: member of the detail. - [bold]Personal Protection Specialist[/bold]: the detail's heavy weapon. - [bold]Personal Protection Coordinator[/bold]: leads the detail and issues its orders.
## Directorate Protection Protects members of the Directorate. It deploys only alongside them, and site staff don't give it orders.
## Standing orders - Protect Company staff, property and research, in that order of convenience. - Colonial law applies on colonial ground. Where the colony's marshals are present, let them be seen to act. - Individuals of interest may be invited to the Company offices to answer questions. Most accept. - Guests stay until the senior employee on site is satisfied. Give them food, water and no reason to complain afterwards. - Force is proportionate, and it's reported. Reports go to Communications before anyone else. - Never discuss an incident with anyone outside the Company. Refer all questions to the Corporate Liaison.
